stem: What is an AI agent in Agentforce?

options.text: An AI assistant that understands a request, decides what to do and takes actions
A fixed script with menu choices

explanation: Agents interpret natural language, choose topics and actions and may take several steps. Scripts and flows follow fixed paths.

stem: How does an agent differ from a flow?

options.text: An agent chooses what to do from natural language, while a flow follows steps you defined
A flow understands natural language, an agent does not
An agent cannot call a flow

explanation: A flow runs the same designed steps every time. An agent decides which topics and actions to use, and can call flows.

objective: Describe the parts of an agent
stem: Which TWO of these are parts of an agent? (Choose 2)
explanation: Agents are built from instructions, topics (or subagents) and actions, and are reached through channels.

objective: Describe the parts of an agent
stem: What is a topic (subagent) in an agent?

options.text: A job the agent can do, with a description, instructions and actions

explanation: Each topic groups a job with the instructions and actions that go with it.

objective: Describe the parts of an agent
stem: Why should a topic have a clear description?

options.text: The agent uses it to decide which topic fits the request
To make the topic visible to users

explanation: The agent reads topic descriptions to pick the right job, so unclear or overlapping topics confuse it.

stem: Which TWO can be the source of an agent action? (Choose 2)
explanation: Actions can be built from flows, prompt templates, Apex and APIs.

stem: An admin already has a refund flow and a case summary prompt. How can an agent use them?
explanation: Existing flows and prompt templates can become actions an agent calls.

stem: Which agent type is aimed at customers and can hand over to a human through Omni-Channel?
explanation: A service agent works with customers and can escalate to a person.

stem: Which agent type helps internal users, for example to summarise a customer?
explanation: Employee agents support staff inside Salesforce or other work apps.

stem: What lets other applications talk to an agent outside the standard channels?
explanation: The Agent API provides a programmatic way to reach an agent from outside standard channels.

stem: What determines which data an agent can read and change?

options.text: The permissions of the user the agent acts as

explanation: An agent acts as a user, and that user's profile and permission sets control access.

stem: An agent exposes data it should not. What should the admin check first?

options.text: The agent user's permissions and the actions' access context

explanation: Too many permissions, system-context flows or over-broad grounding are the usual causes.

stem: Which principle applies when granting permissions to an agent's user?

options.text: Give Modify All Data to avoid errors

explanation: Give the agent only the access it needs, as for any user.

stem: Which is the right order of the agent lifecycle?
explanation: Plan the use case, build it, test it, deploy it, then monitor and improve.

stem: Which tool runs a batch of test requests against an agent before it is released?
explanation: The Testing Center lets you run many test utterances and compare results. Use the conversation preview for quick checks.

stem: Where should an agent be built and tested before reaching customers?

options.text: In a sandbox, then moved to production

explanation: Build and test in a sandbox, then deploy.

objective: Decide when an agent is the right tool
stem: A compliance decision must be identical every time and auditable. Which tool is best?

options.text: An approval process, validation rule or flow

explanation: Rules-based tools give consistent, auditable outcomes. An agent may vary its answer.

objective: Decide when an agent is the right tool
stem: Which request is a good fit for an agent?

options.text: Varied natural-language questions that need several steps and company data
A rule that must always block a save

explanation: Agents suit varied, multi-step requests. Fixed rules and schedules belong to flows, validation rules and approvals.

objective: Decide when an agent is the right tool
stem: What is the best approach when starting with agents?

options.text: Start with one narrow, well-tested job and a human handover

explanation: A narrow, tested use case builds trust and reveals problems early.

stem: What is grounding?

options.text: Giving the agent real company data so answers rely on facts

explanation: Grounding supplies factual, relevant data to the model so it does not guess.

objective: Describe the parts of an agent
stem: What are guardrails?

options.text: Limits that keep an agent safe and on task

explanation: Guardrails include instructions, topic scope, permissions and Trust Layer controls.

stem: How should a customer-facing agent hand over a request it cannot handle?
explanation: Human handover through Omni-Channel keeps customers from getting stuck.

objective: Describe the parts of an agent
stem: Which instruction style works best in a topic?

options.text: Specific and short, saying what to do and what to refuse

explanation: Clear, concise instructions and explicit refusals improve behaviour.
